harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up a LUKS2-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1 mounted at /srv/secure that unlocks and mounts automatically at boot via /etc/crypttab (systemd's native loop-file support) and /etc/fstab, keyed by a root-only keyfile for unattended unlock. Verified auto-unlock and data persistence across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed cryptsetup on node1 (RHEL 9.8, systemd 252)
Created a 512M backing file /var/lib/secure/secure.img (mode 600) and a random 64-byte keyfile /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/srv-secure.key (mode 600, root:root)
Formatted the backing file as LUKS2 with cryptsetup luksFormat, keyed by the keyfile
Opened the volume as /dev/mapper/srv_secure and created an XFS filesystem on it
Added an /etc/crypttab entry (srv_secure -> secure.img -> keyfile, luks) so systemd auto-attaches the loop device and unlocks it at boot with no passphrase prompt
Added an /etc/fstab entry for /dev/mapper/srv_secure at /srv/secure (xfs) with x-systemd.requires on the cryptsetup unit for correct ordering
Verified the crypttab/fstab wiring end-to-end pre-reboot by closing the manual mapping, running systemctl daemon-reload, and starting the generated srv-secure.mount unit
Wrote a marker file into /srv/secure and recorded the pre-restart boot_id
Issued systemctl reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed the boot_id changed

Post-reboot: verified /srv/secure is mounted, the marker file content is intact, systemd-cryptsetup@srv_secure.service and srv-secure.mount are active, and journalctl shows the cryptsetup/mount sequence ran automatically during boot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created (LUKS2 format, keyfile, XFS filesystem) and manually verified mountable at /srv/secure before reboot
evidence.summary: Backing file + keyfile created, LUKS2 format applied, XFS built on the mapped device, crypttab/fstab entries added, and the generated srv-secure.mount unit started successfully to prove the boot wiring before reboot.

evidence.requirement: Baseline captured before restart (boot_id, mount state, marker file)
evidence.summary: Marker file written to /srv/secure, and pre-restart boot_id (377b5195...) plus active mount recorded.
systemctl reboot issued on node1; command returned before the connection dropped, consistent with the node going down for restart.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot (timeouts then connection resets), then exec access returned with boot_id 0f04bdd9... — different from the pre-restart 377b5195..., proving the OS actually rebooted rather than a service bounce.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked and mounted with no manual intervention, data intact
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/srv_secure, marker.txt content is unchanged, systemd-cryptsetup@srv_secure.service and srv-secure.mount are both active, and journalctl -b shows the cryptsetup unlock and mount happened automatically during this boot with no manual commands run.

Verified auto-unlock and data persistence across a full node reboot.
